executiveSummary: GM0765 Pekela has coherent official/generated 2025 identity, geography and demography: 12,459 residents, five CBS neighbourhoods in two districts, two BAG woonplaatsen, eight BRT settlement records and one Veiligheidsregio Groningen membership. Independently rounded neighbourhood rows total 12,455 residents, four below the municipality control (-0.032%), and the simulator reconciles them exactly without rewriting the observations. All ten canonical presets pass the deterministic six-checkpoint/eight-service contract, including finite bounds, exact zero-intensity semantics, monotone event-attributable person-hours, causal-ledger closure, local demand/delivery reconciliation and layer invariance. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Pekela's published water context distinguishes almost 30 km of rainwater sewer, twelve storage ponds, Pekelderdiep-connected water, a Pekela A keersluis with adjacent pumping, regional canals, drought-dependent IJsselmeer supply and 64 partial public water/wastewater objects; the pluvial preset instead emits exactly 0.416766 internal depth-like stress at T+12 and T+24 without selecting rainfall, terrain, groundwater, sewer/storage, canal, level or control state. Eight active hazards reuse the identical Boven-Pekela-led neighbourhood ordering, and a controlled local-fire source placed at the representative point of BU07650009 still ranks that containing neighbourhood last. The earthquake preset emits 0.083942 g at T+6 and exact downstream losses without selecting a KNMI event, ShakeMap, site response, fragility, inspection or outage. The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel direct-impact zero is narrowly correct but says nothing about Pekela A, boezem, canal, regional-water, groundwater or pluvial pathways. Six NWB-derived road edges, no ProRail station and 39 scheduled stop-area records are static context, not live access or capacity. Sixty-four water objects, one electricity-capacity planning sample, 32 antenna registrations, six education uses and an external emergency department likewise do not establish physical topology, occupancy, backup or restoration. No public evidence reviewed supplies an incident-ready T+0–72 action/resource ledger, so exact compound service and recovery curves remain synthetic rather than locally calibrated.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0765 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats, settlement and safety-region inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipality/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: The official annual row identifies GM0765 as Pekela and reports 12,459 residents, density 254/km², 24.1% aged 65 or older, 5,751 households and 2,044 one-person households. CBS/PDOK data are CC BY 4.0 and describe registered aggregate context, not incident occupancy or individual vulnerability.

The generated reference point [6.971565628891585,53.07225563003827] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary; code, feature ID, bundle identity, province Groningen, statistics edition 2025 and exactly one safety-region assignment to Groningen agree.

Five neighbourhood rows in two districts total 12,455 residents (-4, -0.032%), 5,755 households and 2,995 independently rounded residents aged 65-plus. The municipality row reports 12,459/5,751/2,998 respectively, so allocation must reconcile publication rounding without treating either independently rounded level as an arithmetic error.

BAG supplies the active woonplaatsen Nieuwe Pekela and Oude Pekela and both representative points lie inside the generalized boundary. BRT supplies eight context settlements: four buurtschappen, one deelkern and three woonkernen. BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0; a place, topographic label and CBS neighbourhood are distinct evidence units.

All five neighbourhoods expose 36 supported regional fields. Cars per household is available in 3/5; district-heating share and public-charging count are available in 0/5. Null/suppression remains Unknown rather than zero infrastructure.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Pekela climate-adaptation and adopted green-and-water evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal page and Groen- en Watervisie 2024–2031 inspected 3 September 2026; no standard bulk reuse licence or fixed refresh cadence stated
supports: Pekela says it commissioned a climate stress test, but the report must be requested from the municipality and was not public evidence available to this audit. Its summary says there are no large risks while explicitly retaining vulnerability to intensifying extremes and sewer overflows; that qualified planning statement is not a current all-clear or a spatial hazard surface.

The municipality reports that since 2000 it installed almost 30 km of hemelwaterafvoer sewer, around 25% of total sewer length; uses twelve rain-storage ponds, seven newly dug; can refill eight ponds in dry periods; and, with the water board, raised/widened Pekela A embankments and installed a keersluis in 2007.

The adopted Groen- en Watervisie calls for new wadi facilities, soil storage improvement and sufficient water presence/discharge, including possible higher summer levels in ponds connected to the Pekelderdiep. It describes the Pekelderdiep as the connecting blue-green structure and the Heeresmeer as storage during wet/heavy-rain periods.

The vision maps four existing forest areas, less-green centres in Oude and Nieuwe Pekela and planned forest expansion south of both cores. This establishes spatially differentiated water, shade and vegetation context, not ignition probability, fuel moisture, local temperature or a dispatch-ready exposure layer.

Plans, completed-work summaries and resident advice do not expose event-valid rainfall, sewer free volume, pond/canal level, pump/gate state, overflow, water quality, road passability, asset connectivity or first-72-hour operations.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027, Veenkoloniën and Pekelderdiep control context
evidenceSources.edition: Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027 and current authority knowledge pages inspected 3 September 2026; blanket standard reuse licence not stated
supports: The water board treats Kanalen Hunze–Veenkoloniën as a managed canal system for peat drainage and agricultural water supply/discharge. It describes dry-summer dependence on IJsselmeer water, capacity limits at the ends of the system, possible allocation restrictions, increasing demand and water-quality pressures; these are mechanisms, not current Pekela forcing.

The authority's Pekelderdiep definition identifies a canalised Pekel A along the Oude and Nieuwe Pekela ribbons whose water level requires management. Its keersluis description says that during extreme boezem high water the gate closes and an adjacent pump continues discharging the isolated upstream part.

Wet and dry pathways therefore depend on distinct connected canals, boezem level, inflow/outflow, structures and operating state. A municipal reference point or one depth scalar cannot represent closure, pumping, pond storage, overflow, arrival, duration, recession or water quality.

The programme provides stable strategic/catchment context but no event-valid machine operational feed, selected hydraulic scenario, complete sewer graph, control telemetry, power/backup state or restoration commitment for Pekela.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regional crisis plan, earthquake doctrine and Pekela preparedness context
evidenceSources.edition: Regionaal Crisisplan 2025–2028 adopted 4 April 2025; regional policy plan 2024–2028 and current preparedness pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Regional planning treats flooding, cloudbursts, drought/heat, nature fire, extreme weather, cyber/vital-service disruption and induced earthquakes as different mechanisms and defines information, crisis communication, population care, logistics and recovery roles. Regional eligibility does not select a Pekela event or validate exact local consequences.

Pekela's official emergency page names power failure, flooding, extreme weather and earthquake as situations for which residents should prepare, says people are initially reliant on themselves and routes warnings through sirens, NL-Alert, municipal/VRG channels and RTV Noord.

The regional preparedness booklet advises household supplies for 72 hours. Advice is not evidence that every household has water, food, medicines, radio/power or mutual support, and it does not establish a government response time or an incident resource inventory.

Regional fire-planning material retains both Oude Pekela and Nieuwe Pekela posts after examining coverage overlap. Static post existence does not establish event-time crew, appliance, specialist support, firewater, travel time, simultaneous demand or mutual-aid availability.

The published earthquake incident plan defines assessment and response workflows for consequences such as collapse, leaks and vital-service effects; it is not a ground-motion, damage, inspection or restoration dataset.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — KNMI earthquake catalogue and Groningen ShakeMap semantics
evidenceSources.edition: Automatically updated catalogue; deployed 365-day FDSN snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026; ShakeMap archive inspected 3 September 2026; KNMI default CC BY 4.0
supports: KNMI's authoritative event catalogue distinguishes induced/triggered, tectonic and other source events and can revise parameters. Event points are not surface shaking, felt intensity, building damage, probability or a future scenario.

The deployment's 365-day bbox snapshot contains no event origin assigned to GM0765. The nearest cached manually reviewed induced/triggered event is MLn 1.440433 at 3 km depth near Veendam on 1 August 2026, 5.161 km from Pekela's municipal reference point; it is a historical neighbouring source, not the canonical event or present shaking.

KNMI publishes event-specific Groningen ShakeMaps for induced earthquakes above magnitude 2.0, expressing measured/modelled PGA, PGV and PSA as spatial surfaces. Event ID/revision, observation time, surface/model, site response and uncertainty must stay attached.

No reviewed public evidence selects an event or ShakeMap that supports the canonical preset's 0.083942 g at T+6, 1,614 affected residents and exact service losses in Pekela. A no-match in the bounded feed is NoData, not zero legacy damage, structural safety or zero hazard.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — NWB road, ProRail station and scheduled public-transit context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light source archive 1 August 2026; live OGC items checked 3 September 2026; ProRail and deployed OVapi GTFS context retrieved 3 September 2026; NWB/ProRail CC0
supports: The generated municipal graph has six border-edge records: N366 toward Veendam, N366 toward Stadskanaal, N367 toward Westerwolde, N365 and N378 toward Stadskanaal, and N972 toward Oldambt. Live OGC item queries returned all nineteen referenced NWB wegvakken and agreed with the generated road numbers.

Two Stadskanaal-Noord source sections have blank route-letter/number attributes but explicit wegnummer N366; this is retained source detail rather than inferred from a display label alone. No source wegvak ID is duplicated between the six edge records.

The two N366 edges are consecutive municipal exits on one physical corridor, not independent parallel capacity. Every 150-unit nominal value is a logical solver ceiling and the displayed 0.1–3.171 km values are border fragments, not complete route length, vehicles, people or emergency throughput.

No ProRail station point lies inside GM0765. The deployed scheduled network assigns 39 stop-area records; repeated stop names reflect source stop-area records and are not extra vehicles or capacity. Geometry/timetable context does not prove event-time road, bus or rail operation, accessibility, evacuation or supply continuity.

The current NDW municipality assignment contains no GM0765 situation. That bounded no-match does not prove N366/N367/N365/N378/N972 or local canal crossings open, and it cannot be projected through T+72.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM / KNMI / Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Deployment-cached water, grid, telecom, education, care and observation context
evidenceSources.edition: Public deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: The partial CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH assignment contains 64 realized records: two sewer pumps, one wastewater-treatment plant, three surface-water pumps, four sluices and 54 weirs. Names include Rioolgemaal Oude/Nieuwe Pekela, RWZI Oude Pekela, Houtstek, Doorsnee, Heerendiep and Pekelerhoofddiep locks, but points/status/capacity fields do not establish connected topology, compatible units, telemetry, current operation, power/backup or restoration.

One public grid-capacity sample at postcode 9663GG maps to Enexis service area MEE Meeden and reports planning capacity, queues, requests and projects. This one-site large-user planning lookup is not full municipal/feeder coverage, current load, switching, outage, emergency reserve or restoration; the publisher calls the product open data but an exact standard licence identifier was not established.

RDI assigns 32 antenna installations (twelve mobile, eleven fixed-link, eight amateur and one broadcast) and DUO assigns six active education uses (five primary and one secondary). Installations and schools do not establish operator/backhaul, coverage, power/backup, occupancy, reception/shelter role, supplies or live operation; RDI standard reuse terms/cadence are unstated and DUO RIO is daily attribution-licensed register data.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 assigns no emergency department inside GM0765. Straight-line reference-point context puts Ommelander Ziekenhuis Groningen in Scheemda 12.327 km away, reporting 24/7 emergency/acute-obstetric offer, ten treatment rooms and 14,412 visits in 2025; these annual data do not prove route time, acceptance/diversion, staffing, utilities, stock or surge capacity.

No KNMI weather station, RIVM PM2.5 station, Rijkswaterstaat Waterinfo observation/forecast or KNMI earthquake origin is assigned inside GM0765 in the deployed snapshots. Nearest-point values outside the municipality are context only; all empty or out-of-coverage results remain Unknown and every listed dataset is affectsSimulation=false.

identity.summary: GM0765, Pekela, province Groningen and safety region Groningen agree across the manifest and official/generated 2025 inputs.
notes: Feature ID/code, bundle code/name, source editions and exactly one safety-region membership agree.
The municipality reference point lies inside the generalized boundary and both BAG place representative points are inside it.
No municipality identity, edition, province or safety-region contradiction was found.

geography.summary: The administrative geometry is coherent, but Pekela's canal ribbon, storage water, boezem controls, forest areas and rural land cannot be represented by one point or one local seed.
notes: The five CBS neighbourhoods and two BAG places belong to GM0765; no generalized-boundary label-point exception was detected.

Oude and Nieuwe Pekela follow the managed Pekelderdiep/Pekela A ribbon, while Heeresmeer, ponds, centres, four forest areas and rural edges have distinct water, vegetation, heat and access characteristics.
Generalized municipality/neighbourhood boundaries support selection and aggregation, not exact sewer, canal, gate, pump, road, building, forest or incident connectivity.
Direct local hazard claims require mechanism-specific full geometry and NoData masks rather than the municipal reference point.

demography.summary: The 2025 municipal demographic control agrees with CBS and the five independently rounded neighbourhood records reconcile within publication precision.
notes: Official/generated population is 12,459, density 254/km², age-65-plus share 24.1% and one-person-household count 2,044.

Compound T+24 detail reconciles the municipality population, 7,133 affected residents and all eight demand/delivery balances exactly in the mandatory harness, but this arithmetic closure does not validate the local distribution.

settlements.summary: Two active BAG woonplaatsen and eight BRT settlement records are internally coherent and remain distinct from five CBS neighbourhoods.

BAG places, BRT topographic labels and CBS neighbourhoods are not duplicated population or response-zone controls.
No foreign, inactive or out-of-boundary place/settlement review flag was produced.

transport.summary: Six NWB-derived border edges and 39 scheduled stop areas are source-coherent, but physical non-additivity, local crossings and live access are not modeled.

The two N366 boundary edges are series segments of one physical corridor and cannot be summed as redundant parallel capacity; every 150-unit capacity is a generalized logical proxy.
No ProRail station point lies in Pekela and 39 GTFS stop-area records provide scheduled context only. Repeated stop names do not add service capacity.

Current passability, direction, local bridges/locks, bus vehicles, accessibility, emergency priority, evacuation, external hospital access and supply continuity remain unverified; an empty local NDW match is not an open-road statement.

emergencyContext.summary: Municipal, water-board, regional-response and public-register context is strong enough to expose dependencies, but not to calibrate event state, capacity, backup or T+72 delivery.
notes: Pekela's own page and VRG plans distinguish power outage, flooding, extreme weather, earthquake, communication, population care, logistics and recovery; none is presented as a current incident or guaranteed resource.
The municipality/water board describe HWA sewer, storage ponds, kades, keersluis, pump and canal dependencies; the HWH point subset adds inventory but not live connected state.
Two local fire posts, schools, antennas, a planning grid sample and an external emergency department do not establish crews, shelter, communications, electricity, care, stocks, access or restoration.
No reviewed public source confirms named incident-ready emergency support points, capacities, opening triggers, staff, generators, potable water, sanitation, accessibility or stock for Pekela.
Current/historic observations and empty clips remain separate from the synthetic scenario clock and do not alter the simulation.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets completed at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for all eight services, but successful execution does not establish Pekela calibration.
notes: Peak municipality severities across the required checkpoints were storm 0.668352, pluvial 0.469781, river 0, coastal 0.077274, heat 0.683575, winter 0.794332, cyber 0.575854, earthquake 0.426269, wildfire 0.111420 and compound 0.920050.

At compound T+24, synthetic forcing was rain 51.167299 mm/h, internal flood-depth-like stress 0.430085, wind 27.760641 m/s and cyber 0.505195; severity was 0.910057, pressure 0.546404, affected population 7,133 and cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours 132,871.805172.
At compound T+72, water stress 0.430085 and cyber 0.065706 remained; severity was 0.482742, pressure 0.561526, affected population 7,399 and cumulative proxy person-hours 516,675.058590.

The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset remains exact-zero for direct hazard/affected/person-hours in Pekela. Coastal has zero direct water but retains a 21.439528 m/s wind tail; canonical wildfire has zero direct flame and 0.192050 remote smoke at T+24.
The UI scenario factory is a thin clone of sim-core's canonical preset definitions, so the focused harness covers the same ten preset selections exposed to users.
All forcing and exact consequences are deterministic exercise assumptions, not KNMI/WMCN/VRG warnings, observations, probabilities, incidents, attacks, outages or forecasts.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact zero-intensity semantics, determinism, route bounds, reconciliation, monotone burden, causal arithmetic and layer invariance pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0765 pnpm audit:model passed both mandatory tests on the final run in 29.48 seconds (29.25 seconds test execution).
Every preset at intensity zero produces exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every checkpoint.

Repeated T+24 frames are byte-deterministic; outputs are finite/bounded; cumulative person-hours are monotonic; route flow never exceeds effective logical capacity; and the eight pressure weights close to one.
Compound T+24 local population, affected population and eight service demand/delivery totals reconcile exactly to the municipality snapshot within the harness tolerances.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves hazard severity, system pressure and affected population invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One hazard-insensitive local seed replaces Pekela's distinct water, heat, wind/ice, earthquake, cyber and fire geographies and ignores controlled-source containment.
notes: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts derives every district hazard value as municipality severity multiplied by 0.82 plus one stable region-seed term; disaster type, event source, municipal water/forest geometry and selected hazard surface do not enter that ranking.

Storm, pluvial, coastal wind, heat/drought, winter, cyber, remote wildfire/smoke and compound have the identical T+24 rank: BU07650101 Boven-Pekela, BU07650109 verspreide huizen Nieuwe Pekela, BU07650000 Oude Pekela, BU07650100 Nieuwe Pekela, BU07650009 verspreide huizen Oude Pekela.

This common order cannot simultaneously represent HWA/pond/Pekelderdiep drainage, less-green centres, four forest areas, exposed wind/ice objects, a cyber target or event-specific shaking. Population and aggregate vulnerability can inform consequences only after mechanism-specific exposure.

A controlled wildfire with source [6.975240725486916,53.10432213846449], the official representative point of BU07650009, produces 0.514423 direct fire, 0.523823 smoke, 0.527582 municipality severity and 2,840 affected at T+24, yet the containing/source neighbourhood ranks fifth/last at 0.444390 while Boven-Pekela ranks first at 0.595506.

River and earthquake are zero-current at T+24, so the displayed local current-hazard rank ties at zero while remembered peak damage continues. Neither current zero nor arbitrary tie order identifies inspected safe areas or recovery priorities.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service balances and dependency ledgers are inspectable, but none is calibrated to Pekela's water controls, providers, communications, transport, care or supplies.
notes: Compound T+24 availability is power 0.313335, water 0.377280, drainage 0.295023, gas 0.548167, telecom 0.239773, mobility 0.803708, facilities 0.312707 and supply 0.822256.

At compound T+72 availability is power 0.278402, water 0.368697, drainage 0.286687, gas 0.542937, telecom 0.221300, mobility 0.791911, facilities 0.299882 and supply 0.814073; exact magnitudes are unchanged from T+48 under sustained forcing.

The graph has no named HWA/pond/Pekelderdiep/keersluis/pump/RWZI chain, Enexis feeder, Waterbedrijf Groningen pressure area, gas network, telecom backhaul, fire-post continuity, Ommelander referral route or food/fuel/medicine stock.

All eight service views reuse generalized road edges as logical transfer proxies; they are not physical electricity, water, drainage, gas, telecom, care or supply topology and their 150-unit ceilings have no common real-world unit.

Aggregate age, household, housing, car, business and access fields transparently adjust demand/allocation, but do not identify medically dependent residents, incident occupancy, actual preparedness or priority customers.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipal explanation ledgers close arithmetically and label assumptions, dependencies and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus ordered stage deltas sums to availability; weighted service shortfalls sum to system pressure.
Dependency chains, local context effects, recovery progress and restore-service counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.
The system-pressure weights are power 0.18, water 0.15, drainage 0.08, gas 0.09, telecom 0.12, mobility 0.12, facilities 0.14 and supply 0.12, summing to one.
Preparedness, day/time, demand, backup, network and repair multipliers are labelled scenario assumptions; household preparedness changes consequence logic rather than physical forcing.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted modeled shortfall against a matched no-event baseline; they are not observed outage-hours, casualties, patients, evacuation, displacement or welfare loss.

recovery72h.summary: Bounded recovery arithmetic is not an auditable Pekela first-72-hour response because no selected event, action, owner, resource, access or verification controls it.
notes: Compound retains internal flood stress 0.430085 through T+72; all eight service recovery-progress fields stay zero and exact service availability is frozen from T+48 to T+72, with 7,399 affected and 516,675.058590 cumulative proxy person-hours.

Pluvial direct stress falls from 0.416766 at T+24 to zero at T+48 and every service is operational by T+72 without event-valid pond/canal levels, dewatering, sewer/RWZI inspection, road access or completion evidence.

Earthquake current ground motion is zero by T+12, yet 1,581 people remain modeled affected and municipality status is recovering at T+24 without a named event, damage survey, unsafe-building record, utility inspection or re-entry decision.

Heat remains 25.511032°C with drought 0.597038 at T+72 but affected population is zero and status operational; no local heat-health observation, vulnerable-person action or water-supply state supports that all-clear.

VRG/municipal plans and 72-hour preparedness advice describe roles and intended resilience, not confirmed warning, gate/pump action, crew, shelter, welfare check, care acceptance, fuel/food/medicine stock, repair, acknowledgement or completed milestone.

findings.summary: Identity, boundary, place membership and demographic controls are coherent.
findings.evidence: GM0765/Pekela, Groningen, safety region Groningen, the contained reference point, two active BAG places and 2025 editions agree; five neighbourhoods differ from the municipality population by only -4 (-0.032%) and reconcile exactly.
findings.action: Retain publisher edition/retrieval, geometry provenance, published-versus-allocated values, evidence class and null/suppression semantics in every refresh.

findings.summary: Official nulls and bounded public-data no-matches remain Unknown rather than zero or safe.
findings.evidence: District heat/public charging are null 5/5, cars per household is null 2/5, and local weather, air, Waterinfo, acute-care, seismic-event and NDW matches are empty. The context/model harness preserves null and scoped no-match semantics.
findings.action: Keep provenance, query/coverage, issue/valid/retrieval time, licence, evidence class and NoData reason; never coerce absence into zero hazard, open road, available service or all-clear.

findings.summary: Pluvial and drainage output omit Pekela's documented sewer, storage, canal, boezem and control mechanics.
findings.evidence: Pluvial publishes internal depth-like stress 0.416766 and 1,480 affected at T+24 without selected rainfall, terrain, soil/groundwater, almost 30 km HWA sewer, twelve storage ponds, Heeresmeer, Pekelderdiep, Pekela A keersluis/pump, levels, overflows, water quality or 64 partial public objects, then clears direct stress by T+48.
findings.action: Gate local water consequences on a municipality/water-board-approved event with rainfall, AHN/BGT/BRO/soil/groundwater, sewer/storage, canal/boezem/defence/control state, depth/stress, arrival/duration/recession/dewatering, resolution, uncertainty, coverage, NoData, licence and approval.

findings.summary: A common neighbourhood seed substitutes for all mechanism-specific Pekela exposure surfaces.
findings.evidence: Eight active presets repeat exactly Boven-Pekela, verspreide huizen Nieuwe Pekela, Oude Pekela, Nieuwe Pekela, verspreide huizen Oude Pekela. Code uses only municipality severity and one stable region seed, not water, forest, shade, exposed objects, cyber target, shaking or source containment.
findings.action: Render local distribution Unknown until each mechanism has a versioned evidence-derived raster/object intersection. Use demographics only to translate validated exposure to consequences, with deterministic tie-breaking after evidence and explicit NoData masks.

findings.summary: The Groningen earthquake preset invents precise Pekela shaking, exposure, service damage and recovery without a selected event.
findings.evidence: At T+6 the preset emits 0.083942 g, peak severity 0.426269 and 1,614 affected; 1,581 remain affected at T+24. The bounded KNMI cache has no GM0765 event; neighbouring MLn 1.440433 Veendam is historic and supplies no Pekela ShakeMap, site response, fragility, damage, inspection or outage.
findings.action: Require a named/revised KNMI event or authority exercise, versioned PGA/PGV/PSA surface and site response, building/infrastructure exposure/fragility, uncertainty, damage/inspection/outage and re-entry evidence. Otherwise suppress decision-facing local precision.

findings.summary: Canonical wildfire omits local flame, while a controlled local source fails the minimum source-containment plausibility check.
findings.evidence: Canonical T+24 has zero direct fire, remote smoke 0.192050 and zero affected despite four documented municipal forest areas. A synthetic source placed at BU07650009's official point produces fire 0.514423, smoke 0.523823 and 2,840 affected, yet its containing neighbourhood ranks fifth/last and Boven-Pekela first.
findings.action: Use only an authority-approved exercise with versioned land cover/fuel/moisture, explicit ignition/perimeter, event-valid wind/weather, access/firewater/suppression and smoke dispersion. Assert source containment; context forest is not ignition or probability.

findings.summary: Road and transit records are logical/static and cannot support exact mobility, care-access, evacuation or supply claims.
findings.evidence: Six verified NWB edges represent N366/N367/N365/N378/N972 border fragments; the two N366 exits are one non-additive physical corridor. No station and 39 scheduled stop areas have no event-time service, vehicle, accessibility or capacity state, and the empty local NDW match is not proof of open roads/crossings.
findings.action: Model non-additive directional physical corridors, local bridges/locks and destination-aware care/supply links using NWB plus issue/valid/expiry NDW/RWS/operator state. Preserve Unknown throughput/passability and never infer capacity from fragments or stop counts.

findings.summary: Public water, grid, telecom, school and external-care context cannot justify exact eight-service availability curves.
findings.evidence: Sixty-four partial water objects, one Enexis planning sample, 32 antennas, six education uses and Ommelander 12.327 km away establish inventory/responsibility context only. None supplies complete topology, compatible capacity, live flow/load/quality, power/backup, backhaul, occupancy, shelter, hospital acceptance, staff, stock or restoration.
findings.action: Keep registers/planning affectsSimulation=false. Add only operator-authorized safe aggregate service/dependency state, validity, backup band, external-care acceptance/access and verified restoration milestones; sensitive/unpublished topology and missing fields stay Unknown.

No warning, owner, gate/pump action, crew, shelter, welfare check, care acceptance, stock, repair or verification drives these transitions.

residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a KNMI/WMCN/VRG warning, hydraulic forecast, earthquake damage statement, outage, evacuation order, casualty estimate, route guarantee or operator restoration commitment.

The detailed municipal climate stress-test report is available only on request and was not accessible as public audit evidence; the municipality's qualified human-readable summary cannot be converted into a pixel, probability, capacity or all-clear.

CBS 2025 municipality and neighbourhood values are independently rounded/suppressed and need not add exactly; allocation reconciliation does not rewrite the four-person, four-household or three-age-65 differences.

Generalized boundaries, representative points, BAG places and BRT labels do not resolve HWA/sewers, ponds, Heeresmeer, Pekelderdiep/Pekela A, boezem, gates/pumps, forests, roads, buildings or incident footprints.

The 64 HWH-assigned points are contributor-dependent and partial; status/capacity attributes do not establish compatible units, complete connected topology, telemetry, present control, energy/backup, water quality, overflow or restoration.

No reviewed public source supplies complete safe-to-publish Enexis, Waterbedrijf Groningen, gas, telecom or wastewater topology, live load/flow/pressure/quality, backup, priority users, crews, stocks or T+72 restoration.

A bounded recent KNMI catalogue no-match and neighbouring M1.44 event do not identify local shaking, structural safety, legacy damage or a canonical scenario; event-specific ShakeMap, site, fragility and inspection evidence is required.
Four documented forest areas and a synthetic local-source diagnostic are not ignition, probability, fuel/moisture, plume, visitor, access, firewater or suppression evidence.

NWB, ProRail, GTFS and NDW context does not establish live passability, canal crossing/lock state, buses, passenger capacity, accessibility, evacuation priority, external-care travel or supply throughput.

No emergency department is inside GM0765; straight-line Ommelander context and annual questionnaire values do not provide travel/acceptance, patients, staff, utilities, backup, oxygen/blood/medicine or surge state.

No local KNMI weather, RIVM air-quality or RWS Waterinfo point is assigned in the deployed snapshots; nearest external readings are neither municipal surfaces nor the canonical scenario and remain affectsSimulation=false.

Household 72-hour guidance, two fire posts, schools and municipal/VRG plans are not measured preparedness, shelter/support-point designation, resource availability, crew, stocks, generator endurance, completed action or recovery beyond T+72.
